method.method_draft: Read the diagram as showing the original square cut by a horizontal dashed line through its middle, producing two congruent rectangular halves. From the text, the square perimeter is 48 cm, so its side length is 48/4 = 12 cm. Because the cut is halfway across the square, each piece is a 12 cm by 6 cm rectangle. The diagram shows these two pieces placed side by side to form one long rectangle, so the final rectangle is 24 cm by 6 cm. Compute its perimeter as 2(24 + 6) = 60 cm.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a square split into two equal horizontal halves, then rejoined as a rectangle with the two halves touching along their shorter sides. From the text, the square has perimeter 48 cm, so its side is 12 cm. The horizontal cut has length 12 cm, so after cutting, the total perimeter of the two separate pieces is the original 48 cm plus two new cut edges of length 12 cm, giving 72 cm. In the final diagram, the pieces are joined along a vertical internal seam whose length is half the square side, 6 cm. That shared seam is counted twice in the separate-piece perimeter but is not part of the outside perimeter, so subtract 2 × 6 cm from 72 cm to get 60 cm.
method.CoT_raw: Image description: The attached diagram shows a square on the left with a dashed horizontal cut across its middle, making two equal horizontal halves. An arrow points to the right, where the two half-rectangles are placed side by side to form one longer rectangle. In the new rectangle, a dashed vertical line marks the internal seam where the two pieces touch. Reasoning: The original square has perimeter 48 cm, so each side of the square is 48 ÷ 4 = 12 cm. The horizontal cut across the square has length 12 cm, creating two new exposed cut edges, so the total perimeter of the two separate pieces would be 48 + 2 × 12 = 72 cm. In the final rectangle, the two pieces touch along a seam whose length is half the square side, 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm. This seam was counted twice in the separate-piece perimeter but is not on the outside of the final rectangle, so subtract 2 × 6 = 12 cm. Therefore the rectangle’s perimeter is 72 − 12 = 60 cm.
